parts.text: Which claim correctly treats a force as a push or pull between two objects?

options.text: Ojas kicks a football — a push between his foot and the ball.
A ball sits still on grass — the ball applies a force to itself.
Bilal pulls a wagon — the pull acts only on the wagon.
A leaf falls — no objects are interacting.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Charu studies four events: Ojas kicks a football with his foot; a ball sits still on grass; Bilal pulls a wagon; a leaf falls.

part_answers.answer: A force is a push or pull between two objects; the kick is a push between foot and ball.

teacher.key_rationale: A force is a push or pull between two objects. The kick names that pair. A ball does not push itself. A pull is between Bilal and the wagon, not only on the wagon. A falling leaf still interacts with Earth.
